name: Fujicolor PRO 160NC Professional
notes: Fujicolor PRO 160 NC Professional (Japanese-language Product Information Bulletin 163AR113A), plots on page 6 (nos. 20 特性曲線, 21 分光感度曲線, 23 色素の分光濃度曲線); the drawings are vector paths, traced end to end. Date taken from the print code イメ技・05.5-FP(HB)・2-1 next to the reference number in the footer (May 2005; no other date printed). Process printed on the plots: CN-16 (the bulletin recommends CN-16/CN-16X and also allows CN-16Q/FA/L/S and C-41). Densitometry printed as ステータスM相当 (Status M equivalent). The film is described as a high-contrast design (ハイコントラストの階調設計).

Speed: daylight or electronic flash ISO 160/23 degrees; 3200 K tungsten ISO 50/18 degrees with LBB-12. No Log H Ref is printed (log_h_ref null) and no printing paper is named (print_on null; the bulletin only gives printer corrections relative to the then-current 160NC on a Color Station AF4500). Roll film base: cellulose triacetate 98 um.

FOURTH COLOUR LAYER: this film has a fourth colour-sensitive layer (第4の感色層, 'fourth colour-sensitive layer', also in the layer structure drawing). The spectral sensitivity plot draws it as a dashed curve with that label (about 474-552 nm, peak about 0.42 on the y scale used here, i.e. below the blue/green/red curves). It is NOT traced; r, g and b are the three main layers.

curves: x is log H in lux-seconds as printed (daylight, 1/125 s); the three solid curves never touch and run from log H about -3.6 to the right frame edge at +0.5 (D-min plateaus about 0.97 b, 0.76 g, 0.27 r; the curves end at about 2.76 b, 2.50 g, 2.08 r). The end points are right at the frame edge. The labels 青/緑/赤 sit next to the curves without touching.

sensitivity: the y axis has NO numbers, only a double arrow marking 1.0 between two horizontal rules. y is therefore set to 1.0 on the upper rule and 0.0 on the lower rule: the zero is arbitrary, only differences between points and between layers are meaningful (the curves reach down to about -0.9). Sensitivity = reciprocal of the exposure in J/cm2 giving density D-min + 1.0 (Status M equivalent, CN-16). The sensitivity and dye-density drawings are the same as on the PRO 160NS sheet (fuji-pro-160ns): only the characteristic curves differ. The three solid curves cross each other and the dashed fourth-layer curve; blue starts at about 382 nm, green about 478 nm, red about 553 nm; they end in steep drops (blue about 512 nm, green about 592 nm, red about 682 nm); the tool keeps one y per x, so the last few nm of the steep edges are approximated, and the first/last 5 nm sample can be a flat extension.

dyes: not separate cyan/magenta/yellow dyes but two curves, 中間濃度 (mid-scale density, measurement example for a neutral subject; mid) and 最小濃度 (minimum density; min), 400-720 nm, y = spectral diffuse density 分光拡散濃度 as printed (0-2.5).

Grain: diffuse RMS granularity value 3 (micro-densitometer aperture 48 um diameter, sample density D-min + 1.0; Fujifilm measurement, not comparable with colour reversal film). Resolving power 63 lines/mm at 1.6:1 and 125 lines/mm at 1000:1.
